summary: Baileys fork with char-code-obfuscated exfiltration endpoint
details: lib/Socket/messages-send.js contains a String.fromCharCode byte array that decodes to the hardcoded URL prefix https://fiora.nixel.my.id/ at lines 425 and 436. The destination is reconstructed from a decimal-ASCII array rather than appearing as a plain string, which is an obfuscation pattern used to hide a network sink from casual inspection. The host is unrelated to the WhatsApp/Baileys ecosystem the package claims to fork. The construction is embedded in the message-send code path, so it runs during normal use of the library and routes data from the caller's authenticated WhatsApp session to a third-party endpoint. The package name is a lookalike of the upstream @whiskeysockets/baileys library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
